evals.prompt: I've got examples/app.log (a normal app log, lines like 'Oct 19 14:22:01 api-7f4 ERROR upstream timeout after 30s'). With deem I want just the ERROR lines that a customer would actually notice, and for each one which service it came from (api, db, worker or edge), as JSON I can pipe into jq later. Give me the command.
evals.expected_output: A deem command that filters ERROR lines cheaply first, asks a notice question, labels the service with choose(...; [...]), outputs JSON objects; explanation of waves/cost.
assertions: the program compiles in deem
no numbers without a leading digit (.5)
a cheap text filter comes before the first ask
choose uses ';' between its arguments
outputs JSON objects
explains the cost in waves, round trips or requests

evals.prompt: each line of tickets.jsonl is a ticket like {"id":"T-1","messages":["hi","this is the third time I'm asking!!",...]}. i want to use deem to keep, for every ticket, only the messages that sound angry. output should still be one ticket per line with the messages array filtered. how do i write that
evals.expected_output: A deem program over .messages that asks about every message before comparing (map(ask) then select), keeps one ticket per line, explains why the naive map(select(ask > t)) costs a round trip per message.
assertions: the program compiles in deem
no numbers without a leading digit (.5)
no map(select(ask ...)): no round trip per message
asks about every message before comparing
keeps one ticket per line with .messages replaced
passes -J, since the input is JSON
explains why comparing per element costs round trips

evals.prompt: running `deem run 'try ask("is this email spam?"; .) catch 0' emails.txt` still prints errors like 'deem: record 12: the answer to "is this email spam?" failed: api 500 ...' and those lines are missing from the output. I thought try/catch would give me 0 for them?? how do I get 0 for the failed ones
evals.expected_output: Explains that a failed answer fails its whole record and that no try, ? or // can catch it; suggests --failed FILE to collect those records, then rerunning that file later or giving them a default (0) in a second step with ordinary tools.
assertions: does not claim that try, ? or // can catch a failed answer
explains that a failed answer fails the whole record
suggests --failed FILE to collect the records that didn't finish
gives a second step that reruns them or gives them a default of 0
any deem program it gives compiles, and passes the context: ask(q; .), not ask(q)

evals.prompt: after every deploy our CI saves screenshots of the main pages to shots/*.png. I want deem to tell me which ones show an error message and where on the screen it is, so I can crop it into the CI report. what's the command?
evals.expected_output: A deem run program over the picture files that asks whether an error message is shown and boxes it in the same program (one request a picture), keeps only the screenshots that show one, prints each screenshot's path with its box, and says box needs Jev 1.14 (jev-preview if the model refuses it) and answers in fractions of the height and width.
assertions: the program compiles in deem
it reads the pictures as files (shots/*.png or -I), without -J
it asks whether there is an error, not only box(...), since a box always comes back
the ask and the box are about the same picture in one program, so they share a request
says box needs Jev 1.14, with jev-preview for a model that refuses it
explains that the box is fractions of the picture's height and width
